key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr coatings, higher-velocity spray processes produced denser, harder coatings with better wear and corrosion performance than atmospheric plasma spraying.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-critical components, HVOF and HVAF emerge as the strongest coating choices on 304 stainless steel in this study.
method: Prepared WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, hardness, wear behavior, and electrochemical corrosion resistance.
Ranked performance across spray routes to identify the best process windows.
evidence_signal: Hardness increased from 771.4 HV (APS) to about 1166 HV (HVOF/HVAF), while wear rate dropped from 36.82×10^-5 mm3/N·m for bare steel to 1.10–1.17×10^-5 for HVOF/HVAF coatings; HVAF also showed the best corrosion metrics.
watch_item: Results are process- and parameter-dependent, so the reported ranking may shift with spray settings, substrate condition, or service environment.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
